rationale: Additive CNS depression/anticholinergic burden increases fall and delirium risk, especially in older recipients on baseline immunosuppression-related fatigue.
transplant_relevance: General, not transplant-specific, but elevated baseline risk in this population.

rationale: Additive bleeding risk from dual antiplatelet or antiplatelet+anticoagulant combinations.
transplant_relevance: Relevant post-transplant for vascular access/cardiac comorbidity management -- see antiplatelet_vascular_exception in protocol rules; not automatically safe just because it is common.

rationale: Additive QT-prolongation risk from stacked QT-prolonging agents.
transplant_relevance: Transplant patients frequently carry multiple QT-prolonging agents simultaneously (antifungals, antiemetics, some antibiotics) -- worth explicit tracking rather than folding into generic duplicate-therapy severity.

example_drug_pairs: NSAID + CNI; aminoglycoside + CNI; IV contrast + CNI
rationale: Additive nephrotoxicity risk directly threatens graft function -- higher stakes than generic nephrotoxicity in a non-transplant patient.
transplant_relevance: High priority for transplant cohort specifically -- graft loss risk, not just generic AKI risk.

rationale: CNIs already predispose to hyperkalemia via distal tubule effects; additive agents (trimethoprim, ACEi/ARB, potassium-sparing diuretics) compound this.
transplant_relevance: Transplant-specific because CNI baseline effect changes the risk calculus versus a non-CNI patient on the same combination.

rationale: A monotonic dose-decline pattern is a planned taper, not duplicate therapy -- see steroid_planned_taper in protocol rules. Should REDUCE concern once the taper pattern is confirmed, not increase it.
transplant_relevance: Directly transplant-relevant; this was the vignette-6-adjacent finding from the elicitation pilot.

example_drug_pairs: azole antifungal + statin; multiple hepatotoxic agents
rationale: Additive hepatotoxicity risk from combined CYP-interacting/hepatotoxic agents.
transplant_relevance: Relevant given how often transplant patients are on statins, azoles, and TMP-SMX simultaneously.

rationale: Additive serotonergic activity increases serotonin syndrome risk. Tramadol and meperidine are the opioids with well-established serotonergic activity; fentanyl's serotonergic risk is weaker and more disputed in the literature -- flag fentanyl+SSRI/linezolid at lower confidence, do not treat identically to tramadol.
transplant_relevance: General risk, elevated relevance if patient has comorbid depression/anxiety management common post-transplant.
